rationale: The trivariate VAR (step 8) produced results/trivariate_var.json and figures/fig7_trivariate_irf.png from the 1978-1990 LAUS window (n_obs=663). The employment IRF builds to a peak magnitude of -0.02121 (-2.1%) at year 3 (year 4 = -0.02069 = -2.1%), matching the paper's '-2.0 percent after four years' to within ~6% relative error (near the match threshold). The reported employment_plateau (year 12) is -0.01809 (-1.8%) versus the paper's -1.3%, a ~39% relative deviation (no_match on this component); the summary attributes some of this to the documented approximation that the unemployment/participation responses are proxied as -le/lp with working-age population proxied by resident population (see trivariate_var.json 'note' and evidence_summary documented_approximations). For the disappearance horizon, unemp_partic_dieout_year gives participation=7 (within the paper's 5-7 range) and unemployment=11 (beyond it) -- though the raw unemployment IRF is tiny throughout (peak ~0.002 = 0.2pp) and effectively near zero by year 5-6. Overall the qualitative structure and the peak match well and participation dieout matches, but the plateau magnitude and the unemployment horizon deviate, so the composite claim is graded partial. fix_severity.json records no critical fixes in this path (one minor networking patch, one major elasticity-alignment fix in a different step).
